items.stem: What is the key difference between equality and equity?

options.text: Equality gives everyone the same; equity adjusts support to needs and barriers
options.rationale: Correct: equity accounts for different starting points and barriers.

options.text: They mean exactly the same thing
options.rationale: They are related but distinct concepts.
Equality is one notion of fairness, not its absence.

items.stem: Which actions help reduce bias in a hiring process? (Select TWO)

options.text: Using structured, consistent interview questions for all candidates
options.rationale: Correct: structure reduces the influence of unconscious bias.

options.text: Defining job-relevant criteria before reviewing candidates
options.rationale: Correct: pre-set criteria guard against post-hoc rationalisation.

options.text: Relying on an informal 'culture fit' gut feeling
Assuming a neutral-seeming process needs no examination
options.rationale: Processes can embed systemic barriers despite appearing neutral.

items.explanation: Correct: structure reduces the influence of unconscious bias.

items.stem: A company publishes a strong DEI statement but changes none of its practices. What does this illustrate?

options.text: A statement is not the same as measured, sustained action
options.rationale: Correct: real change requires action and honest measurement, not words alone.
Statements without action do not change outcomes.
Progress can be tracked with meaningful measures.

options.text: Everyday behaviour is irrelevant to DEI
options.rationale: Inclusive behaviour is central to real change.
